claim_text: The state says an unauthorized user accessed myColorado platform data
summary: Colorado says that late on Wednesday Nov 18 it found a cybersecurity incident in the myColorado app 'where an unauthorized user was able to access platform data'.
detail: This is in the FAQ on the official myColorado.gov page, which the state's Office of Information Technology (OIT) runs. The Record reports the same from OIT. The state has not said how the user got in, beyond saying its teams are working to 'fix the vulnerability'.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's own page says an unauthorized user accessed platform data.
notes: Tier 1: read on mycolorado.gov on Nov 25.

claim_text: The state shut the app down when it found the incident and began investigating
summary: The state says it shut down the app as soon as it found the incident, to protect Coloradans' data and state systems, and began investigating.
detail: The Record reports OIT shut down the app and began an investigation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's FAQ says so directly.

claim_text: The myColorado app is still unavailable, with no restoration date
summary: As of the state's Nov 25 update, the app remains unavailable. The state says its teams are running security tests on security enhancements before relaunching the app, and it has no confirmed restoration timeline.
detail: The myColorado.gov banner still said on Nov 25 that the app is currently unavailable, and the state promises daily updates. KRDO and The Record also report it offline on Nov 24.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's page says the app will remain temporarily unavailable and gives no date.
notes: Re-read myColorado.gov on every check: this is the service claim.

claim_text: The state estimates roughly 100,000 users' data was involved
summary: The state says it currently estimates that roughly 100,000 users' data was involved, out of about 2.1 million app users, and that it will refine the estimate as it matches the accessed documents to individual users.
detail: Until Nov 24 the state gave a range of 50,000 to 150,000 people; its Nov 25 update gives roughly 100,000 instead. The Record's Nov 24 report says 'nearly 150,000 people'.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's FAQ, updated Nov 25, gives the estimate in these words.
notes: Changed Nov 25: was the state's 50,000 to 150,000 range, which its page no longer shows.

claim_text: The app has about 2.1 million users
summary: The state says myColorado has approximately 2.1 million users. It holds digital driver licenses and IDs and links to state services.
detail: The Record repeats the state's figure.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's FAQ gives the user count.

claim_text: Exactly whose documents were accessed is not yet known
summary: The state says staff are still matching the accessed documents to individual users, so exactly whose data was involved is not yet known.
detail: The state says the notices it sends will name the specific documents or files involved for each person.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The state's Nov 25 FAQ says the matching is still going on.
notes: Until Nov 25 this claim said what data was accessed was not known; the state's Nov 25 update now says which kind of data (c011).

claim_text: Who got in, and how, is not known
summary: The state has not said who the unauthorized user was or how they got in. Its Nov 24 update speaks of fixing 'the vulnerability' without describing it.
detail: The state says its automated threat detection in its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud environment flagged unusual usage, and its security team then found what appeared to be unauthorized activity. It has not said how the user got in. No group has claimed it in anything we read. We did not open leak or dark-web sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources names an attacker or a method.

claim_text: The state says it has no reason to think this is part of a bigger attack
summary: Asked whether this is related to broader cyberattacks, the state says: 'We don't have any reason to believe that this is a part of a bigger attack.'
detail: This is the state's own word; nobody independent has examined it. The Record mentions other government incidents the same week for context and does not link them.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The state's FAQ says this in these words.

claim_text: Users should carry their physical ID; state services are still available on agency websites
summary: The state asks users to use their physical driver license or state ID, including at airports, and to reach state services through agency websites such as the DMV's while the app is down.
detail: It says Colorado law requires carrying a physical ID even when using a digital one. Users planning to use a mobile driver license at the airport can add it to another DMV-approved digital wallet, the state says.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's update and FAQ give this advice.

claim_text: Some users can still open their digital ID in airplane mode, because the app caches it
summary: The state explains that some users can still bring up their digital ID in airplane mode because the app stores some data on the phone so it works without a connection.
detail: Some data may not be cached if it was not opened recently or the app was reinstalled. This explains reports that the ID still shows; it is not a sign the service is back.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's FAQ explains it directly.

claim_text: The state says the incident mainly involved documents users had uploaded to the app, not payment information
summary: The state says the incident primarily involved the app's 'myCards and Documents' section: user-uploaded PDFs and photos of documents such as passports, vehicle registrations and insurance cards. Payment information was not involved.
detail: The state posted this on Nov 25. It advises users to change matching passwords, turn on two-step sign-in, watch bank accounts and consider a free credit freeze.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's own FAQ, updated Nov 25, says which part of the app and which kinds of documents were accessed, and that payment information was not.
notes: Tier 1: read on mycolorado.gov on Nov 25.

claim_text: The state expects to start notifying affected users on Nov 27
summary: The state says people whose data was involved will be notified directly, with the specific documents or files involved for each person, and that it expects the notices to begin going out on Friday, Nov 27.
detail: Denver7 reports the same date from the state.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's FAQ, updated Nov 25, gives the date and says what the notices will contain.
notes: A dated promise: check whether notices have gone out after Nov 27.
